scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You swallow a small tablet for a headache, and somehow it knows where the pain is. Does it?

scenes.name: everywhere
scenes.text: It doesn't. The medicine dissolves, enters the blood, and spreads through the whole body.

scenes.name: prostaglandins
scenes.text: Injured tissue makes chemicals called prostaglandins, which make nerves more sensitive and cause swelling.

scenes.name: nsaid
scenes.text: Drugs like ibuprofen block an enzyme called COX, so fewer prostaglandins are made where it hurts.

scenes.name: paracetamol
scenes.text: Paracetamol works mainly in the brain and spinal cord, and scientists still don't fully understand how.

scenes.name: brain
scenes.text: Pain is the brain's reading of nerve signals. Calm the signals, and the pain feels smaller.

scenes.name: safety
scenes.text: Follow the dose on the label, and ask a doctor or pharmacist if unsure. This is general info, not medical advice.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Spread, block, quiet the signal. Follow for more on how things really work.
